api_function: Retrieve the complete list of assignments. The response contains a collection of Assignment objects, each including commit information (date/time and descriptions), and nested Employee and Project details (e.g., employee credentials, department/location, contact and job info, and project dates/status). This supports organizational project tracking and oversight by exposing assignment records across projects and employees.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint accepts no path parameters, query parameters, or request body; the request body must be empty. A valid authenticated context (e.g., Authorization credentials) is required; otherwise a 401 Unauthorized may be returned. Appropriate permissions/roles are required to access assignment data; insufficient privileges may yield 403 Forbidden. Set an Accept header such as application/json (or */*) to receive the JSON payload. Filtering, pagination, and sorting parameters are not supported on this endpoint; it always returns the full collection.

api_function: Update an existing assignment in the project tracking system. The client sends a full Assignment JSON to modify commit/progress details (e.g., commitDate, employee/manager notes) and/or the linked employee and project information (by IDs and/or embedded objects). On success, returns the updated Assignment; may return 201 if an upsert-style create occurred; 401/403 for auth issues; 404 if the target resource does not exist.
parameters_constraints: Request body is required and must be a JSON object representing an Assignment. Field-level constraints: commitDate: string in the exact pattern dd-MM-yyyyHH:mm:ss (two-digit day, '-', two-digit month, '-', four-digit year, then two-digit hour 00–23, ':', two-digit minute 00–59, ':', two-digit second 00–59; no space between date and time). commitEmpDesc, commitMgrDesc: free-form strings (text notes). employee: object; if provided, its fields follow: employee.employeeId: 32-bit signed integer (typically positive). employee.firstName, employee.lastName, employee.job: strings. employee.email: string that should be in a valid email address format. employee.phone: string (telephone text, digits/symbols allowed). employee.hiredate: string in pattern dd-MM-yyyy. employee.salary: number (double precision, typically non-negative). employee.credential: object with credentialId (int32), enabled (boolean), username (string), password (string), role (string). employee.department: object with departmentId (int32), departmentName (string), and location (object). employee.department.location: object with locationId (int32), adr (string), city (string), postalCode (string). employee.credentialId/departmentId/locationId should fit 32-bit signed integer range (commonly positive). employee.email/phone/password/username/role/departmentName/adr/city/postalCode are strings without a prescribed max length in the spec. employeeId (top-level): 32-bit signed integer (commonly a positive existing employee identifier). project: object; if provided, its fields follow: project.projectId: 32-bit signed integer (commonly positive existing project identifier). project.title, project.status: strings. project.startDate, project.endDate: strings in pattern dd-MM-yyyy. projectId (top-level): 32-bit signed integer (commonly positive existing project identifier). Booleans must be true/false; numbers must be valid JSON numbers; integers must not exceed int32 range. Dates must match the indicated patterns exactly; invalid or differently formatted dates are likely to be rejected.

api_function: Create or save an assignment record that links an employee to a project and optionally captures progress/commit information (commit date and employee/manager descriptions). The request can include either simple identifiers (employeeId, projectId) and/or embedded employee and project objects; the API persists the assignment and returns the saved Assignment representation.
parameters_constraints: The request body 'assignment' is required and must be application/json. For single-field constraints: commitDate must be a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyyHH:mm:ss (day-month-year followed immediately by 24-hour time, e.g., 31-12-2025 235959 without a separator per example) and represent a valid date-time; commitEmpDesc and commitMgrDesc are free-text strings. Numeric identifier fields employeeId, projectId, employee.employeeId, credential.credentialId, department.departmentId, location.locationId, and project.projectId must be 32-bit integers (int32). In the embedded Employee object: email should be a syntactically valid email address; hiredate must be a string in dd-MM-yyyy format representing a valid calendar date; phone is a string holding a phone number; salary must be a number in double precision (non-negative values are typically expected in this domain); credential.enabled is boolean (true/false); credential.username and credential.password are non-empty strings; credential.role is a string that should match a valid system role identifier. In the embedded Department object: departmentName, and location fields adr, city, postalCode are strings, and locationId is int32. In the embedded Project object: startDate and endDate must be strings in dd-MM-yyyy format; status and title are strings. All string fields should be UTF-8 text; where values represent codes (e.g., role, status), they must be valid identifiers recognized by the system. Each field must conform to its declared type/format irrespective of whether only IDs or full nested objects are supplied.

api_function: Retrieve the full collection of assignment records accessible to the caller. Each assignment includes commit/progress descriptions, commit date-time, linked employee details (including credential, department, and location info), and linked project details (title, status, start/end dates). This endpoint supports organizational project tracking by listing all assignments.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any input parameters (no path, query, or request body fields). The request must use the GET method and typically requires a valid authenticated/authorized context; otherwise it may return 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden). If an Accept header is provided, it must be compatible with a JSON response (the API advertises */*).

api_function: Retrieve all project commit/progress entries for a specific employee within a specific project. The response contains a collection of ProjectCommit objects including commitDate (date-time), employee and manager commit descriptions, the employee's first and last name, and the corresponding employeeId and projectId. Requires authentication and appropriate authorization (401/403 on failure); returns 404 if the resource is not found.
parameters_constraints: Both path parameters are required. employeeId: must be a non-empty numeric identifier consisting only of digits, representing a positive 32-bit signed integer (1 to 2,147,483,647) that matches an existing employee record. projectId: must be a non-empty numeric identifier consisting only of digits, representing a positive 32-bit signed integer (1 to 2,147,483,647) that matches an existing project record. Each value should be provided without whitespace, separators, or leading signs; if the identifier does not exist, the request can result in a 404 Not Found.

api_function: Retrieve a single project commit/progress record for a specific employee on a specific project made at a given commit date/time. On success, returns a ProjectCommit object containing the commit timestamp, employee and manager descriptions, employee and project IDs, and the employee’s first and last name.
parameters_constraints: All three path parameters are required and must be non-empty. The parameter employeeId must represent a valid employee identifier as a numeric int32 value expressed in the URL (positive integer within 1–2147483647, no leading/trailing spaces or non-digit characters). The parameter projectId must represent a valid project identifier as a numeric int32 value expressed in the URL (positive integer within 1–2147483647, digits only). The parameter commitDate must be a valid ISO 8601 date or date-time string that matches the stored commit’s timestamp (e.g., YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ); if a time portion is included, ensure characters such as ':' or '+' are properly URL-encoded or use a 'Z' UTC designator. Any format or value that does not correspond to an existing commit for the given employee and project may result in a 404 Not Found, and missing/invalid authentication may yield 401/403.

api_function: Retrieve all commit/progress update records for a specific project. For the given project identifier, the API returns a collection of project commit entries including commit date/time, employee- and manager-provided descriptions, the contributing employee's ID and name, and the associated project ID. Intended for project tracking and management views.
parameters_constraints: projectId (path) is required and must be a non-empty, URL-safe identifier that uniquely identifies an existing project. Although defined as a string in the path, it typically represents a numeric project ID (int32) encoded as text; provide only the canonical project ID value (no spaces or slashes). If the value does not correspond to a project, a 404 Not Found may be returned. The caller must be authorized to access the specified project; otherwise, 401/403 may occur.

api_function: Deletes an assignment/commit record in the project tracking system identified by the employeeId, projectId, and commitDate. This is used to remove a specific employee’s assignment or progress/commit entry for a given project on a particular date. Successful deletion returns 200 (optionally with a response body) or 204 (no content), while 401/403 indicate authentication/authorization failures.
parameters_constraints: All three path parameters (employeeId, projectId, commitDate) are required, non-empty strings supplied as separate URL path segments. The commitDate must be a valid calendar date in ISO 8601 date format YYYY-MM-DD (no time component). The employeeId must be a valid identifier of an existing employee, and the projectId must be a valid identifier of an existing project. For path safety, each value must not contain the '/' character, should not include leading or trailing whitespace, is case-sensitive as provided, and must be URL-encoded if any reserved characters are present.

api_function: Create or update an assignment that links an employee to a project within the project tracking system. The endpoint accepts an Assignment payload containing optional employee and manager commit/progress descriptions and a commit timestamp, and it can carry nested employee/project details or their IDs. On success it returns the saved Assignment (200) or indicates a new resource was created (201). Authentication/authorization errors yield 401/403; missing referenced resources may yield 404.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be a JSON object conforming to the Assignment schema. Field-level constraints: commitDate must be a string representing a valid date-time (day-month-year with 24-hour time and seconds), e.g., dd-MM-yyyy HH:mm:ss, with HH in 00–23 and mm/ss in 00–59; the date part must be a real calendar date with months 01–12. commitEmpDesc and commitMgrDesc are free-text strings. employee (object), when provided, must match: credential (object) with credentialId as a 32-bit integer, enabled as boolean, and password/role/username as strings; department (object) with departmentId as a 32-bit integer, departmentName as string, and location (object) with locationId as a 32-bit integer and adr/city/postalCode as strings; email should be a valid email-address string; employeeId as a 32-bit integer; firstName and lastName as strings; hiredate as a date string in dd-MM-yyyy (valid calendar date); job as string; phone as a string representing a telephone number; salary as a finite double precision number, preferably non-negative. employeeId (at the Assignment root) is a 32-bit integer. project (object), when provided, must match: projectId as a 32-bit integer; startDate and endDate as date strings in dd-MM-yyyy (valid calendar dates); status as string; title as a non-empty string. projectId (at the Assignment root) is a 32-bit integer. General constraints: all ID fields are integers (int32) and should be positive whole numbers; salary is a number (double) and should not be NaN or infinity; date strings must follow the indicated patterns; strings used as identifiers or titles should avoid leading/trailing whitespace. The request content type should be application/json.

api_function: Update an existing assignment record that links an employee to a project, along with commit/progress details and related employee/project metadata. The endpoint accepts an Assignment JSON payload and returns the updated Assignment object on success. It may respond with 401/403 for authentication/authorization issues and 404 when the target assignment/resource is not found.
parameters_constraints: Request body is required and must be application/json representing an Assignment object. Field-level constraints: commitDate must be a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyyHH:mm:ss (valid calendar date and time). commitEmpDesc and commitMgrDesc are free-text strings. Top-level employeeId and projectId, as well as all *_Id fields within nested objects, are 32-bit integers and should be positive integers. employee (object): employeeId (int32); email should be a syntactically valid email address string; firstName, lastName, job, phone are strings; hiredate is a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyy (valid calendar date); salary is a numeric double (non-negative number). employee.credential (object): credentialId (int32), enabled (boolean true/false), password (string), role (string), username (string). employee.department (object): departmentId (int32), departmentName (string), location (object) with locationId (int32), adr (string), city (string), postalCode (string). project (object): projectId (int32), title (string), status (string), startDate and endDate are strings formatted as dd-MM-yyyy (valid calendar dates). All boolean fields must be true/false literals; numeric fields must be valid numbers; strings should be provided as text values. The request must be sent with Content-Type: application/json.

api_function: Retrieve all assignment records for a specific employee within a specific project, returning a collection of assignments that include commit/progress notes and embedded employee and project details.
parameters_constraints: Both path parameters are required and must be non-empty. employeeId must be a numeric string that represents a positive 32-bit integer (1 to 2147483647) identifying an existing employee; non-digit characters, decimals, or negative values are invalid and may result in 400/404 errors. projectId must be a numeric string that represents a positive 32-bit integer (1 to 2147483647) identifying an existing project; non-digit characters, decimals, or negative values are invalid and may result in 400/404 errors. Values must be URL-safe (no encoding-unsafe characters or whitespace).

api_function: Retrieve a specific assignment commit/progress record by its composite key: employee ID, project ID, and the exact commit timestamp. The response includes commit details (e.g., employee and manager comments), along with related employee and project information. Returns 404 if no matching record is found, and requires proper authentication/authorization.
parameters_constraints: All three path parameters are required and must be non-empty. employeeId: must be a positive integer identifier (32-bit range) represented as digits in the path (e.g., 123), referring to an existing employee. projectId: must be a positive integer identifier (32-bit range) represented as digits in the path (e.g., 45), referring to an existing project. commitDate: must be a valid date-time string matching the pattern dd-MM-yyyyHH:mm:ss with zero-padded components and no separator between date and hour (e.g., 08-05-202401:30:00), where dd is 01–31 (valid for the month/year), MM is 01–12, yyyy is a four-digit year, HH is 00–23, mm is 00–59, and ss is 00–59. As path segments, values should not contain leading/trailing spaces or slashes; URL-encode any special characters if needed. The combination must match an existing commit record to avoid 404.

api_function: Deletes an assignment record (or a dated assignment/commit entry) in the project tracking system, identified by the composite key made up of employeeId, projectId, and commitDate. Intended for removing an employee’s assignment or its dated progress/commit entry from a project.
parameters_constraints: All three path parameters are required, must be non-empty URL-safe strings, and must exactly match existing records in the system. employeeId: a string identifier for an existing employee; typically a UUID or numeric ID used by the service. It must not contain slashes or unencoded reserved characters. projectId: a string identifier for an existing project; typically a UUID or numeric ID used by the service. It must not contain slashes or unencoded reserved characters. commitDate: a string representing a valid calendar date in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD), with zero-padded month and day (e.g., 2025-04-01). It should represent the date under which the assignment/commit entry was stored. Because these are path parameters, any reserved characters must be percent-encoded and whitespace should be avoided.

api_function: Authenticates a user by validating the provided username and password. On successful authentication (200 OK), it returns an object containing the username and a boolean isEligible flag indicating whether the authenticated user is eligible to access protected resources. Requests with missing or invalid credentials typically result in 401 Unauthorized; authenticated users lacking required permissions may receive 403 Forbidden; 404 may indicate the account or related resource was not found.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a JSON object with two string fields: username and password. For effective authentication: (1) username must be provided as a string and should be a non-empty identifier corresponding to an existing account in the system (null or missing values are invalid). (2) password must be provided as a string and should be non-empty; it is treated as an opaque, case-sensitive secret (null, missing, or empty values are invalid). Both fields must be encoded as JSON strings; providing other data types or omitting either field will likely cause authentication to fail with 401 Unauthorized.

api_function: Authenticates a user for the project tracking and management system by validating supplied credentials. On successful validation, returns 200 OK with the username and a boolean isEligible flag indicating whether the authenticated account is eligible to access protected resources. If credentials are invalid, the server responds with 401 Unauthorized; a 403 Forbidden may indicate a valid account that lacks permission or is blocked.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing two string fields: username and password. username: must be a non-empty JSON string that exactly matches an existing account identifier in the system; comparison is exact and typically case-sensitive. password: must be a non-empty JSON string that exactly matches the stored secret for the given account; it is case-sensitive. Each field must be provided as a string (not null, not numeric/boolean/array/object). Empty strings or missing fields will prevent successful authentication and lead to an unauthorized response.

api_function: Retrieves all stored access credentials. On success it returns a collection of Credential objects (each including credentialId, username, role, enabled, and password) wrapped in a DtoCollectionCredential. This list is typically used by administrators to view or manage user access within the project tracking and management system.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept path, query, or request-body parameters. The client should not send a request body. A valid authentication context (e.g., Authorization header) is required; otherwise the server may return 401 (Unauthorized). The caller must have sufficient privileges to read credentials; insufficient privileges may result in 403 (Forbidden). The response is returned as JSON (generic */* content type advertised).

api_function: Update an existing credential record (username, password, role, enabled) in the system. Clients submit a Credential object in the request body; on success, the API returns the updated Credential (200). Depending on implementation, if the payload represents a new record it may create it (201). The endpoint enforces authorization (401 if unauthenticated, 403 if not permitted) and may return 404 when the referenced credential cannot be found.
parameters_constraints: Request body must be a JSON object shaped as Credential. Field constraints: credentialId must be a 32-bit integer (int32); for an update it should be a positive integer referencing the target credential (non-fractional, not a string). enabled must be a boolean (true or false); null is not allowed. username must be a string; it should be non-empty and is typically unique in the system (avoid leading/trailing whitespace). password must be a string; it should be non-empty and comply with the system’s password policy (e.g., minimum length/complexity), and must not be null. role must be a string that matches one of the system-defined roles (e.g., ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE); values outside the allowed set will be rejected. Extra or incorrectly typed fields may lead to validation errors (400).

api_function: Create or save a user access credential in the system. The endpoint accepts a Credential object (username, password, role, enabled, and optionally credentialId) and persists it. When creating a new credential it may return 201 Created; when saving/updating it may return 200 OK, along with the saved credential payload.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing an object that matches the Credential schema. Field-level constraints: credentialId must be an integer within 32‑bit range and, as an identifier, should be a positive number when provided (typically omitted for new creations). enabled must be a boolean value (true or false). password must be a string and should not be empty or whitespace-only given its authentication purpose. role must be a string and should match a valid role recognized by the system (e.g., an administrator, manager, or employee role name; exact allowed values are system-defined). username must be a string and should be non-empty; in practice it is expected to be unique within the system. Unknown or incorrectly typed fields may result in validation errors.

api_function: Delete a credential by its identifier. Clients provide a credentialId in the query string to request removal of the corresponding access credential. On success the API may return 200 with a boolean (indicating the deletion result) or 204 with no content; 401 indicates the caller is not authenticated, and 403 indicates insufficient permissions.
parameters_constraints: credentialId (query): required. Must be a non-empty string that uniquely identifies an existing credential record. It should strictly follow the system’s identifier format (commonly a UUID string: 36 characters with hyphens in 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal segments). Do not include leading/trailing whitespace, spaces, or control characters; use only valid identifier characters (hex digits and hyphens if UUID). If numeric IDs are used internally, they must still be supplied as a string value in the query.

api_function: Retrieve the complete list of access credentials in the system. The response wraps a collection of Credential objects (credentialId, username, role, enabled, password) in a DtoCollectionCredential, intended for administrative oversight and management of user access within the organizational project tracking platform.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any request parameters (no path, query, or body inputs). Clients should issue a GET request to the exact path and not include a request body. Access likely requires valid authentication/authorization; unauthorized or forbidden requests will return 401 or 403 respectively. If authorized, a 200 response returns a JSON object containing a 'collection' array of credentials.

api_function: Deletes a credential record by its identifier. Clients pass the credentialId in the query string; if the caller is authorized, the service attempts to remove the matching credential. On success it may return 200 OK with a boolean indicating the outcome, or 204 No Content when no body is returned. 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden indicate authentication/authorization failures.
parameters_constraints: credentialId (query, string) is effectively required to perform the deletion. It must be a non-empty string that exactly matches the unique identifier of an existing credential in the system. The value should conform to the system’s credential ID format (often a UUID) and be properly URL-encoded if it contains reserved characters. Leading or trailing whitespace should be avoided, and the identifier is case-sensitive if the system treats IDs as such. If credentialId is missing, empty, malformed, or does not correspond to any stored credential, the deletion cannot succeed.

api_function: Create or update an access credential in the organizational project tracking system. The endpoint accepts a Credential object (username, password, role, enabled flag, and optional credentialId) and persists it, returning the saved credential on success. It is intended for managing authentication/authorization data (e.g., admin-maintained user accounts and roles).
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be an application/json object of type Credential. credentialId must be a 32-bit signed integer; typically a positive value when updating an existing credential and omitted when creating a new one. enabled must be a boolean value (true or false). username must be a non-empty string representing the login identifier and is expected to be unique within the system. password must be a non-empty string; provide it at account creation and whenever changing the password, conforming to any server-side password policy. role must be a string that matches one of the system’s allowed roles (for example, ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE); values outside the configured role set will be rejected.

api_function: Update an existing access credential record in the system. Administrators or authorized users can modify properties of a credential (username, password, role, enabled) identified by its credentialId. On success, the updated Credential object is returned.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a Credential object. The field credentialId must be provided as a 32-bit signed integer (positive value) identifying an existing credential; if it does not match an existing record, the server may respond with 404 Not Found. The field enabled, if provided, must be a boolean (true or false). The field password, if provided, must be a non-empty string and should comply with the system’s password policy (e.g., minimum length and complexity). The field role, if provided, must be a string that matches one of the system’s valid roles; values outside the predefined role set will be rejected by the service’s validation. The field username, if provided, must be a non-empty string that conforms to the system’s username rules and should be unique within the system. All fields must match their declared data types; sending a mismatched type (e.g., a string for enabled) will cause the update to fail.

api_function: Retrieve a credential record by username. Given a username in the path, the API returns the corresponding credential object (credentialId, enabled, password, role, username). If the caller is not authenticated or lacks permission, it returns 401/403; if no credential exists for the supplied username, it returns 404. This is used within the organization’s project/assignment management system to look up access credentials.
parameters_constraints: username (path) is required and must be a non-empty string that exactly matches a stored username; otherwise a 404 Not Found is returned. As a path segment, it must be URL-safe: do not include raw '/' characters (they must be percent-encoded) and percent-encode any reserved characters (such as space, '#', '?', '%', '+', '@'). Avoid leading or trailing whitespace; if present, it will be treated literally and likely not match any account. Case sensitivity is not specified—do not assume case folding; supply the username in the exact case as stored.

api_function: Delete the access credential record associated with the specified username. This endpoint removes credentials by username and returns a boolean indicating whether the deletion occurred. It is part of the credential management resources within the organizational project tracking system and requires appropriate authorization; unauthorized or forbidden requests are rejected.
parameters_constraints: username is a required path parameter and must be a non-empty string. It must be provided as a single URL path segment (must not contain '/' characters). Any spaces or special characters must be URL-encoded; avoid unintended leading or trailing whitespace. The value should exactly identify the target account's username as stored by the system (case and characters must match the stored value). No explicit length or character set constraints are defined in the spec; therefore, provide a valid, system-recognized username to achieve successful deletion.

api_function: Retrieve a specific credential record by its identifier. On success, it returns a Credential object containing credentialId, username, role, enabled status, and password. If the caller is not authenticated or lacks permission, the request is rejected; if the identifier does not correspond to an existing credential, it is not found.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter id is required and must be a non-empty string provided as a single URL path segment. It should be treated as an opaque, case-sensitive identifier that exactly matches an existing credential in the system; otherwise a 404 Not Found is returned. The value must not contain unescaped reserved URL characters (e.g., '/') and should be URL-encoded if special characters are present. Leading/trailing whitespace should be avoided, and the parameter cannot be null or omitted; unauthorized access may yield 401/403 regardless of id value.

api_function: Retrieve all departments. Returns an object with a collection array of department records, each containing departmentId (int32), departmentName (string), and a location object (adr, city, locationId int32, postalCode). Useful for admins/managers to view the department catalog within the organizational project tracking system.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept path, query, or body parameters. Access typically requires valid authentication/authorization; requests without proper credentials can result in 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden. Ensure the request includes the appropriate Authorization header (e.g., a valid bearer token) and an acceptable Accept header for JSON responses.

api_function: Update an existing department resource. Clients send a Department JSON object (including its identifier and any fields to update, such as name and nested location details). On success, the service returns the updated Department; if an upsert is supported it may return 201 Created, while 404 indicates the target department was not found.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json matching the Department schema. Field-level constraints: departmentId must be a 32-bit integer (int32) and should be provided to identify the department to update; use a positive whole number that corresponds to an existing department to avoid 404. departmentName must be a string; provide a non-empty, meaningful name. location (optional) must be an object; if present, its fields must match their types: adr is a string, city is a string, postalCode is a string, and locationId is a 32-bit integer (int32). Avoid including unknown or malformed fields and ensure all provided values respect their declared types. Set the Content-Type header to application/json for the request body.

api_function: Creates (saves) a department record in the system, optionally including location details. The endpoint accepts a Department JSON object and returns the persisted Department. It is part of the organization/project management service where admins manage departments; authentication/authorization is typically required (401/403 on failure). The server may return 201 (created) or 200 (ok) depending on implementation.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json with a top-level object named Department. Field-level constraints: departmentId must be an integer in 32-bit signed range (−2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647); for new creations it is typically omitted or null, and if provided it must conform to int32. departmentName must be a string; to be meaningful it should be a non-empty, trimmed textual name (null is not acceptable for creating a usable department). location, if provided, must be an object containing any of the following fields: adr (string), city (string), postalCode (string), and/or locationId (32-bit signed integer). Each string field should be valid UTF-8 text; if present, it should not exceed typical application limits (no explicit max length is defined here). Each integer field must fit within 32-bit signed integer bounds. Property names are case-sensitive and only the documented fields should be included. The overall payload must be valid JSON; missing request body or wrong content type will cause a client error.

api_function: Deletes a department by its identifier. Intended for administrative management of organizational structures; when provided a departmentId, the endpoint attempts to remove the corresponding department and responds with a boolean result or no content. Unauthorized or forbidden requests are rejected.
parameters_constraints: Query parameter departmentId is required and must be a non-empty string that uniquely identifies the target department to delete. It must match the system’s identifier format (e.g., a canonical ID such as a UUID if that is what the service uses) and correspond to an existing department; otherwise deletion will not succeed. The value should be provided exactly as stored (case-sensitive if applicable), without leading/trailing whitespace, and must be URL-safe when sent in the query string.

api_function: Retrieve all departments. The endpoint returns a collection of Department objects, each including departmentId, departmentName, and a nested location with adr, city, locationId, and postalCode. Useful for administrators and managers to view available departments within the organizational project tracking system.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; the request body must be empty. Use the GET method only. A valid authentication credential may be required; otherwise the service can return 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden). The client should request JSON (e.g., via an Accept header) to receive the structured department collection.

api_function: Deletes a department identified by its unique ID. The client supplies the departmentId as a query parameter, and the service attempts to remove that department record. A successful attempt returns a boolean (often true) with 200 OK, or may return 204 No Content; 401/403 indicate lack of authorization. This is used by administrators in the organization/project management system to manage departments.
parameters_constraints: departmentId (query, string) is effectively required even though not explicitly marked; it must be a single, non-empty string representing the unique identifier of the department to delete. It must conform to the system’s ID format (commonly a stable identifier such as a UUID or database-generated string) and should be provided exactly as stored (avoid leading/trailing spaces). The value must reference an existing department; otherwise the deletion will not proceed and the response may indicate no deletion occurred. No request body is used and only this single ID is accepted in the query.

api_function: Create or update a Department resource in the organizational management system. The endpoint accepts a JSON body describing a department (including an optional nested location object) and returns the saved Department. A 201 response indicates creation of a new department; a 200 response indicates an update to an existing one. Authentication may be required, as indicated by possible 401/403 responses.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json matching the Department schema. Field-level constraints: departmentId must be a 32-bit signed integer (int32). It is optional; when supplied it should identify the department to update, and when omitted a new department is typically created. departmentName must be a string; provide a non-empty, human-readable name for the department. location is an optional object; if provided its fields must conform to: location.locationId as a 32-bit signed integer (int32); location.adr as a string; location.city as a string; location.postalCode as a string (keep as string to preserve any leading zeros). All numeric fields must be valid JSON numbers within the int32 range (−2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647). String fields should be sent as JSON strings and should not be null. Field names are case-sensitive and must match the schema.

api_function: Updates a department resource by accepting a Department object and returning the updated Department. Typical use is to modify a department’s name and/or its location details. The request body is required. On success it returns 200 with the updated object; if the server creates the department during the operation it may return 201. Requests may fail with 401/403 for auth issues or 404 if the target cannot be found.
parameters_constraints: The request body must be application/json and contain a Department object. Field constraints: departmentId must be an integer in 32‑bit signed range (int32); for updates it should be provided and typically be a positive identifier. departmentName must be a string; it should be non-empty human‑readable text (avoid null/blank values). location, if provided, must be an object with the following fields: locationId as a 32‑bit signed integer (int32, typically positive); adr as a string for street/address; city as a string for city name; postalCode as a string (free‑form postal/ZIP code text, may include letters, digits, and symbols such as hyphens). No other types are allowed for these fields, and values must conform to their declared types.

api_function: Retrieve a single department by its unique identifier and return its details. On success, the API responds with a Department object containing departmentId, departmentName, and a nested Location object (adr, city, locationId, postalCode). This is used within the organizational project tracking and management system to look up department records.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter id is required and must be provided as a non-empty URL path segment. Although defined as a string in the path, it is expected to represent the department’s numeric identifier (departmentId is int32 in the response), so it should consist only of digits and represent a positive 32-bit integer (1 to 2147483647). It must not include slashes, spaces, or unencoded special characters (URL-encode if necessary). Leading and trailing whitespace should not be present. The value must correspond to an existing department; otherwise, a 404 Not Found response is returned. Requests without proper authentication or authorization may receive 401/403 respectively.

api_function: Retrieve the full list of employees. The response wraps a collection of Employee objects that include personal fields (firstName, lastName, email, phone, hiredate as a string formatted like dd-MM-yyyy, job, salary), identifiers (employeeId), and nested structures for credential (credentialId, enabled, username, role, password) and department (departmentId, departmentName, and location with locationId, adr, city, postalCode). Used by the organizational project tracking/management service for admins/managers to view employees and their organizational context.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; it is an unfiltered list operation. Clients must be authenticated and authorized to access it (unauthenticated requests result in 401 Unauthorized; insufficient permissions result in 403 Forbidden). Provide an Accept header capable of handling JSON responses (e.g., application/json). No pagination, sorting, or filtering parameters are defined in the specification.

api_function: Updates an employee resource by accepting a full Employee object and returning the updated record. It can modify personal details, contact info, hire date, job, salary, department/location associations, and login credentials. A successful update returns 200; creation semantics may occur in some cases (201). Requests require authorization (401/403 on failure) and a missing target may yield 404.
parameters_constraints: Request body employee is required and must be application/json matching the Employee schema. employeeId must be a 32-bit integer (int32) identifying the employee to update. firstName, lastName, job, email, and phone are strings; email must be a valid email address format. hiredate must be a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyy (day-month-year) and represent a valid calendar date. salary must be a JSON number (double-precision); it should be finite and non-negative. credential (if provided) must be an object with: credentialId as int32, enabled as boolean, password as string (subject to system password rules), role as a string matching a valid system role, and username as string. department (if provided) must be an object with: departmentId as int32, departmentName as string, and location (if provided) as an object with locationId as int32, adr as string, city as string, and postalCode as string. All id fields (employeeId, credentialId, departmentId, locationId) must be 32-bit integers. The Content-Type header must be application/json.

api_function: Create (save) an employee resource in the organizational project management system. The endpoint accepts a JSON Employee object that may include personal details, employment info, department and location association, and access credentials. On success, it returns the persisted Employee object (201 Created or 200 OK). Authentication/authorization may be required (401/403).
parameters_constraints: Request body is required and must be application/json representing an Employee object. Each property is optional unless enforced by server-side rules, but when provided must match its type/format: employeeId: 32-bit integer. firstName: string. lastName: string. job: string. email: string (free-form; provide a valid email string if the server validates it). phone: string (free-form). hiredate: string representing a date; example suggests dd-MM-yyyy, so supply a valid calendar date in that pattern if enforced. salary: number in double precision (finite numeric value; decimals allowed). department: object with the following optional fields—departmentId: 32-bit integer; departmentName: string; location: object with locationId: 32-bit integer, adr: string, city: string, postalCode: string. credential: object with the following optional fields—credentialId: 32-bit integer; enabled: boolean (true/false); username: string; password: string; role: string. All integer fields must be whole numbers within 32-bit signed range; boolean must be true or false; strings must be JSON strings; numeric fields must not be NaN/Infinity. Provide only types consistent with the schema to avoid 400 Invalid Input.

api_function: Deletes an employee resource by its identifier. The client supplies the employeeId as a query parameter, and the service attempts to remove the corresponding employee. A 200 response returns a boolean indicating the outcome, 204 indicates no content, and 401/403 indicate authentication/authorization failures.
parameters_constraints: employeeId (query, string) must be provided to target a specific employee for deletion; it should be a non-empty string that exactly matches a valid, existing employee identifier issued by the system (e.g., the ID returned when the employee was created). The value should be URL-safe/URL-encoded as needed, contain no leading or trailing whitespace, and be supplied as a single value (not multiple values). If the identifier does not exist or is malformed, the deletion will not succeed.

api_function: Retrieve the complete collection of employees. On success, returns an object with a 'collection' array where each element is an Employee including personal fields (employeeId, firstName, lastName, email, phone, job, hiredate, salary) and nested objects for credential (credentialId, enabled, username, role, password) and department (departmentId, departmentName, location with adr, city, postalCode). This is used in the organizational project tracking and management service for administrators and managers to view all employees and their organizational context.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint accepts no path, query, or body parameters; do not send a request body. A simple HTTP GET to the exact path '/app/api/employees/' is required. The caller must provide valid authentication and have permission to access employee resources; otherwise 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden) may be returned. Use a standard Accept header that can handle JSON responses (e.g., application/json).

api_function: Retrieve all employees that belong to the specified department. On success, it returns a collection of employee records including employeeId, first/last name, job, email, phone, hire date, salary, their department (departmentId, departmentName, and location details), and credential metadata (credentialId, enabled, password, role, username). Authentication is required; requests may be rejected with 401/403 if unauthorized, and 404 if the department does not exist.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter departmentId is required and must be a non-empty value. Although declared as a string in the path, it represents the department's numeric identifier and should be a sequence of digits that can be parsed as a 32-bit signed integer (positive, within int32 range). It must correspond to an existing department to receive a 200 response; otherwise a 404 Not Found may be returned. If any non-alphanumeric characters are used, they must be URL-safe or properly URL-encoded.

api_function: Retrieve all project assignment records for a specific employee. Given an employeeId, the API returns a collection of EmployeeProjectData entries that include projectId, title, status, startDate, and endDate, enabling project tracking for that employee. Authentication/authorization is enforced (401/403), and a 404 is returned if the employee or their project data is not found.
parameters_constraints: employeeId (path, required) must be a non-empty string placed in the URL path in place of {employeeId}. It must be URL-safe (no slashes; special characters must be percent-encoded), should not contain leading or trailing whitespace, and must conform to the system’s employee identifier format (typically an alphanumeric or UUID-like value). The value is case-sensitive and must correspond to an existing employee accessible to the caller; otherwise the request may result in 404 or authorization errors.

api_function: Retrieve the set of manager-related project records associated with a specific employee. Given an employee’s identifier, the API returns a collection of projects with fields such as projectId, title, status, startDate, and endDate. Intended for organizational project tracking contexts, it supports authenticated access and will return 404 if the employee does not exist.
parameters_constraints: employeeId is a required path parameter and must be a non-empty string that uniquely identifies an employee in the system. Because it is part of the URL path, it must not contain forward slashes and must be URL-encoded if it includes special characters. It should match the system-defined employee identifier format (e.g., a UUID or an alphanumeric employee code) and refer to an existing employee; otherwise, the request will result in a 404 Not Found. Leading/trailing whitespace should be avoided.

api_function: Deletes an employee record by its identifier. The client supplies the employeeId as a query parameter; if authorized, the service attempts to remove the corresponding employee resource. On success it may return a boolean in a 200 response or 204 No Content. Requests without proper authentication or permissions return 401/403.
parameters_constraints: employeeId (query, string) is functionally required to perform deletion. It must be a non-empty, trimmed string that exactly matches a valid employee identifier issued by the system (use the ID returned by employee creation/list APIs). Preserve exact characters and casing; URL-encode if the ID includes characters that require encoding in a URL. The value must reference an existing employee record for the deletion to succeed; providing a missing or invalid ID will result in no deletion (e.g., a false boolean or no content).

api_function: Create or update an employee record (including personal details, salary, department association, location, and access credentials) and return the persisted Employee. On success, the service may respond with 200 (updated/returned) or 201 (created); authentication/authorization is enforced.
parameters_constraints: Request body is a JSON object representing an Employee. employeeId: 32-bit integer; typically omitted or null when creating a new employee, and a positive existing ID when updating. firstName and lastName: non-empty trimmed strings; avoid leading/trailing whitespace. email: string that should be a valid email address format. hiredate: string in exact dd-MM-yyyy format (two-digit day, two-digit month, four-digit year) and must be a real calendar date. job: non-empty string (often chosen from predefined job titles in the system). phone: phone-number string; digits with optional leading + and separators are typically accepted. salary: double-precision number; should be non-negative. credential.credentialId: 32-bit integer; positive when referencing an existing credential record; omit for new credentials. credential.enabled: boolean (true or false). credential.password: non-empty string that should satisfy the system’s password policy (e.g., minimum length and complexity). credential.role: string expected to match one of the predefined roles in the system (e.g., ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE). credential.username: non-empty string; should be unique within the system; case handling depends on server policy. department.departmentId: 32-bit integer; positive and should reference an existing department. department.departmentName: free-text string (used when name is required or displayed). department.location.locationId: 32-bit integer; positive and should reference an existing location. department.location.adr, department.location.city: free-text strings. department.location.postalCode: string; should follow the postal code format of the location’s country. All unspecified fields are optional unless server-side validation enforces them; additional unknown properties are typically ignored or rejected depending on server configuration.

api_function: Update an existing employee record (and optionally its nested credential, department, and location details) in the organizational project tracking system. On success it returns the updated Employee (200). Some implementations may create the record if it does not exist (201). Requests without proper authorization may be rejected (401/403), and updating a non-existent employee may return 404.
parameters_constraints: Request body is required and must be application/json representing an Employee object. employeeId must be a 32-bit integer (positive) identifying the employee to update; for a typical update it should reference an existing record. email must be a syntactically valid email string. firstName, lastName, and job should be non-empty strings when provided. hiredate must be a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyy (e.g., 05-09-2025). phone is a string; provide a valid phone number format (digits with optional leading + and separators). salary must be a numeric double and should be non-negative. credential is an object: credentialId is a 32-bit integer (positive) if referencing existing credentials; enabled is boolean; username is a non-empty string; password is a string (non-empty if changing it); role is a string that should match an allowed role in this system (e.g., ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE). department is an object: departmentId is a 32-bit integer (positive) if referencing an existing department; departmentName is a non-empty string if supplied. department.location is an object: locationId is a 32-bit integer (positive) if referencing an existing location; adr, city, and postalCode are strings (use non-empty values when provided). All integer fields use 32-bit range, boolean fields accept only true/false, and strings should not exceed reasonable lengths for their domain. Unknown or type-mismatched fields may cause validation errors. Ensure idempotent updates typical of PUT by sending the full intended state for fields you wish to persist.

api_function: Retrieve an employee record by login username. On success, it returns an Employee object containing credential details (username, role, enabled, etc.), personal and job information (firstName, lastName, email, phone, job, salary, hiredate), and organizational context (department with location). Used to look up employee details within the organizational project tracking and management system.
parameters_constraints: Path parameter username is required and must be a non-empty string representing the employee’s login username. It must be provided as a single path segment (no unencoded slashes) and should be URL-encoded if it contains spaces or reserved characters. Leading/trailing whitespace should not be included. The value must correspond to an existing username in the system to receive 200; otherwise 404 is returned. Authentication/authorization may be required (401/403) but do not change the format requirements of username.

api_function: Deletes an employee resource identified by its unique username. Intended for administrative/management operations in the organizational project tracking system. On authorized requests, the endpoint attempts to remove the employee matching the supplied username and may respond with 200 (boolean indicating whether a deletion occurred) or 204 (deletion with no response body), with 401/403 for authentication/authorization failures.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter username is required and must be a non-empty string representing the exact unique username of the employee to delete. It must be provided as a single URL path segment (cannot contain '/'); any reserved or special characters (e.g., spaces, '+', '@') must be URL-encoded. Case matching may be significant; supply the username exactly as stored. Leading/trailing whitespace should be avoided (trimmed) to prevent mismatches. The value must correspond to an existing employee username for the deletion to take effect; otherwise the operation may complete without deleting any record.

api_function: Retrieve a single employee by identifier and return the employee’s full profile, including core fields (employeeId, firstName, lastName, email, phone, job, salary, hiredate) and nested objects such as credential (username, role, enabled) and department with location details.
parameters_constraints: id is a required path parameter and must be supplied in the URL. It must be a non-empty, URL-safe string that represents a valid employee identifier. Although defined as a string, it is expected to correspond to the system’s employeeId (an int32), so it should typically be a decimal numeric value within the 32-bit signed integer range (1–2147483647) with no extra characters or whitespace. If the identifier does not correspond to an existing employee, the API will respond with 404 Not Found.

api_function: Retrieve the full list of Location resources. On success, it returns an object containing a collection (array) of Location entries, where each entry includes locationId (integer), adr (address string), city (string), and postalCode (string). This is used to list available locations within the organizational project tracking and management system.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; the request body must be empty. Clients should not supply extraneous parameters as they are not supported. Access requires valid authentication and appropriate authorization; missing or invalid credentials can result in 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden responses. The response is JSON; an explicit Accept header is optional as */* is supported.

api_function: Update a location resource in the organization/project management system by sending a Location JSON object. It modifies fields such as address (adr), city, and postalCode for the location identified by locationId. On success it returns the updated Location (200). If the payload is treated as a new entity it may be created (201). If the specified location does not exist, the server may return 404. Requests require authorization (401/403 on failure).
parameters_constraints: The request body location is required and must be application/json with an object matching the Location schema. locationId must be an int32 value; for an update it should be a positive integer referring to an existing record. If locationId is missing or null, the server may create a new location (resulting in 201); if provided but not found, 404 may be returned. adr is a string; when provided it should be a non-empty textual street address. city is a string; when provided it should be a non-empty city name. postalCode is a string; when provided it should be a non-empty postal/ZIP code (may include letters, digits, and separators as appropriate for the locale). Only the defined fields (adr, city, locationId, postalCode) are expected; extra properties may be ignored or rejected. Set the Content-Type header to application/json.

api_function: Create or save a Location resource in the organization/project tracking system. Clients submit a Location object (address, city, postal/ZIP code, and optionally an identifier) and receive the persisted Location back on success (200 OK) or a creation acknowledgment (201 Created). Authentication/authorization is enforced (401/403 on failure).
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json representing a Location object. Field constraints: adr: string; represents the street address; if provided, it should be a non-empty textual value (no null), trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace. city: string; represents the city name; if provided, it should be a non-empty textual value (no null). postalCode: string; represents the postal/ZIP code; if provided, it should be a textual value; use a valid code for the relevant locale (letters/digits, spaces or hyphens commonly allowed). locationId: integer (int32); if provided, it must fit the signed 32-bit integer range (−2147483648 to 2147483647); typically omitted when creating a new location and included when saving an existing one. Only the defined fields should be sent; unknown types or type mismatches (e.g., non-string in adr/city/postalCode, non-integer in locationId) will cause validation errors.

api_function: Deletes a location resource by its identifier. This endpoint removes the specified location from the organizational project tracking system.
parameters_constraints: Query parameter locationId is required to perform the deletion. It must be provided in the query string as a non-empty string and is treated as the exact, opaque identifier assigned by the system to a location. The value should match an existing location’s ID, be supplied without leading or trailing whitespace, and not be a list or multiple values (only a single ID is accepted). Use standard URL encoding for the query value if necessary.

api_function: Retrieve all location records. Returns a collection wrapper (DtoCollectionLocation) containing an array of Location objects, each with adr (address), city, postalCode, and locationId (int32). Used within the project/organization management system to list available locations.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; the request body must be empty. Access typically requires valid authentication (e.g., an Authorization credential) as indicated by possible 401/403 responses. Clients should request a JSON response (e.g., via an appropriate Accept header).

api_function: Deletes a location resource by its identifier in the organizational project tracking system. Typically used by authorized users (e.g., admins/managers) to remove an existing location record. Successful deletion may return 200 (OK) or 204 (No Content); 401/403 indicate authentication/authorization failures.
parameters_constraints: locationId (query): required. Must be a non-empty string that uniquely identifies a location in the system. It must conform to the service’s identifier format (e.g., a UUID-like or numeric/string ID used by the locations resource) and refer to an existing location to be deleted. Avoid leading/trailing whitespace; provide a URL-safe value exactly as stored. An absent, empty, or malformed identifier will prevent a valid delete operation.

api_function: Create or update a Location resource within the organization/project management system. The endpoint accepts a Location JSON payload (adr, city, postalCode, and optionally locationId) and persists it. Typically returns 201 Created when creating a new Location and 200 OK when updating an existing one, responding with the saved Location object.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be a JSON object representing a Location. Field constraints: (1) locationId: integer (32-bit). Must be a whole number without decimals. Commonly omitted or null for creation; when provided it should refer to an existing Location and be a positive integer for updates. (2) adr: string. Should be a textual street/address line; provide a non-empty string rather than null or whitespace-only content. (3) city: string. Provide a non-empty city name; typical characters include letters, spaces, and hyphens. (4) postalCode: string. Provide a non-empty postal/ZIP code; format is region-dependent and generally alphanumeric; avoid unsupported special characters. All string fields must be valid JSON strings (not numbers/arrays/objects). The content type should be application/json, and the payload should only include serializable values matching the declared types to avoid validation or persistence errors.

api_function: Updates an existing location record in the project tracking system. The client submits a Location object (address, city, postalCode) identified by locationId. On success the API returns 200 with the updated Location. Requests require authentication/authorization (401/403 on failure), and a 404 is returned if the referenced location does not exist. The API may also respond with 201 Created depending on server behavior.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a Location object. The field locationId is required, must be a 32‑bit integer (no decimals or quoted strings), should be a positive value, and must identify the location to update; if it does not correspond to an existing record, a 404 Not Found may be returned. The fields adr, city, and postalCode, if provided, must be strings; the schema does not define formats or length limits, so they should be sent as plain strings suitable for address, city name, and postal/ZIP code. Valid authentication credentials and sufficient permissions are required, otherwise the request will fail with 401/403.

api_function: Retrieve a single Location resource by its identifier within the project/organization management system. On success, returns details such as address (adr), city, postalCode, and an internal numeric locationId.
parameters_constraints: id is a required path parameter of type string. It must be a non-empty, URL-safe value that exactly matches an existing location’s identifier (treat as an opaque, case-sensitive string). Any reserved or special characters must be percent-encoded; slashes must not appear unless encoded. Leading/trailing whitespace is not ignored and should not be included. If the identifier does not correspond to an existing record, the API returns 404.

api_function: Retrieve all projects. The endpoint returns a collection of Project objects used in the organizational project tracking and management system, each containing projectId, title, status, startDate, and endDate.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or request body parameters; calls should be made without a request body. A valid authenticated request is likely required (401 Unauthorized and 403 Forbidden are possible outcomes). The expected response is JSON; providing an appropriate Accept header (e.g., application/json) is recommended.

api_function: Update an existing project by submitting a JSON Project object. This endpoint is used in the project tracking system for managers (or authorized users) to edit project details such as title, status, startDate, and endDate. On success it returns the updated Project (200); it may return 201 if the server treats the request as an upsert/creation, 401/403 for authentication/authorization failures, and 404 if the target project cannot be found.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a Project object. The field projectId must be a 32‑bit integer (int32), typically a positive value identifying the project to update and expected to correspond to an existing project (otherwise 404 may occur). The field title must be a non‑empty string representing the project’s name (avoid null or blank values). The field status must be a non‑empty string and should match one of the system’s predefined status values (e.g., a recognized lifecycle state; values outside the allowed set will be invalid). The fields startDate and endDate must be strings formatted exactly as dd‑MM‑yyyy (two‑digit day 01–31, two‑digit month 01–12, four‑digit year), must represent valid calendar dates, and must not include time or timezone components (e.g., 25‑12‑2025).

api_function: Create or save a project resource. Clients submit project details (title, status, start/end dates, optional projectId) and receive the persisted Project object in response. Used by the project tracking system for managers to create or update projects.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be a JSON object representing a Project. Field constraints: projectId must be a valid 32-bit integer (int32); when creating new projects it is typically omitted, and if provided it must be a valid integer value. title must be a string; provide a meaningful, non-empty project name. status must be a string; it should align with server-supported project lifecycle states (arbitrary values may be rejected). startDate must be a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyy (two-digit day, two-digit month, four-digit year, hyphen-separated) and represent a valid calendar date. endDate must be a string formatted as dd-MM-yyyy and represent a valid calendar date. Only the defined fields should be sent; unspecified or malformed types (e.g., non-string dates, non-integer projectId) may cause validation errors.

api_function: Delete a project by its identifier. This endpoint removes a project resource from the organizational project tracking system when provided with a valid project ID. Successful deletions return 200 or 204; unauthorized or forbidden requests return 401 or 403 respectively.
parameters_constraints: Query parameter projectId is a string and must be supplied to identify the project to delete. It should be a non-empty, exact project identifier recognized by the system (typically a system-generated unique ID), treated as case-sensitive and without leading/trailing whitespace. If it contains special characters, it must be URL-encoded. The deletion will only succeed if the provided projectId corresponds to an existing, deletable project.

api_function: Retrieve the full list of projects available to the authenticated user in the organizational project tracking system. The response includes a collection of Project objects with fields such as projectId, title, status, startDate, and endDate.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; clients should not send a request body. The HTTP method must be GET and the path must be exactly /app/api/projects/ (including the trailing slash). A valid authentication context is required (requests without proper credentials may receive 401 Unauthorized; insufficient permissions may result in 403 Forbidden). A 404 Not Found may be returned if the resource is unavailable.

api_function: Deletes a project identified by its ID in the project tracking/management system. On success it returns 200 OK or 204 No Content. Requests require authentication, and lack of authentication or permission results in 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden.
parameters_constraints: projectId (query, string) is effectively required to specify which project to delete. It must be a non-empty string that exactly matches a valid, existing project identifier issued by the system. Provide the ID exactly as stored (case-sensitive), without leading/trailing whitespace, and URL-encode any special characters since it is passed in the query string. Only IDs belonging to the authenticated account/organization will be eligible for deletion under the caller’s permissions.

api_function: Save (create or update) a project in the organizational project tracking system. The endpoint accepts a Project JSON payload and returns the saved Project. It requires authentication and may return 401/403 on authorization failures, 200 on success, and 201 when a new resource is created.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be a JSON object representing a Project with the following self-constraints for each field: (1) projectId must be a 32-bit integer (whole number within the signed 32-bit range; do not quote or include decimals). (2) title must be a non-empty string; leading/trailing whitespace should be avoided. (3) status must be a string that matches a valid system-defined project status (e.g., PLANNED, ACTIVE, ON_HOLD, COMPLETED, CANCELLED); unrecognized values may be rejected. (4) startDate must be a string formatted exactly as dd-MM-yyyy, using two-digit day, two-digit month, and four-digit year with hyphen separators (e.g., 05-09-2026); it must be a real calendar date and must not include time or timezone. (5) endDate must be a string formatted exactly as dd-MM-yyyy with the same rules as startDate. The Content-Type of the request should be application/json, and field names must match the schema exactly.

api_function: Update an existing project in the organizational project-tracking system. Clients submit a JSON Project payload containing the target projectId and any fields to modify (title, status, startDate, endDate). On success it returns the updated Project (200). Requests require authentication (401/403 on failure), and a non-existent projectId results in 404.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a Project object. projectId: a required 32-bit integer that must be a positive value identifying an existing project in the system. title: a string; if provided, it should be a non-empty, trimmed name for the project. status: a string; if provided, it must match one of the system-defined project status values (only predefined values are accepted; values are case sensitive). startDate and endDate: strings that, if provided, must be valid calendar dates formatted as dd-MM-yyyy (two-digit day, two-digit month, four-digit year, e.g., 05-09-2026). Invalid or improperly formatted dates are not accepted. Fields not relevant to the Project schema should not be included.

api_function: Retrieve a specific project's details by its identifier. This authenticated endpoint returns the project's metadata (title, status, startDate, endDate, and the numeric projectId) for tracking and management purposes.
parameters_constraints: Path parameter id is required and must be a non-empty, URL-safe path segment representing a valid project identifier. Although defined as a string, it is implicitly expected to be a decimal numeric string corresponding to the internal int32 projectId; therefore it should contain digits only, with no sign, spaces, or formatting characters, and represent a positive 32-bit integer (1–2147483647). An id that does not correspond to an existing project will result in 404 Not Found; access without proper authentication/authorization may yield 401/403.
